candidates.exact_span: 4Q3        Lowest four-day average flow rate expected to occur once every three-years
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defines the flow statistic used when permit limits or monitoring conditions are keyed to low-flow or design-flow events; a different reading of the averaging period or recurrence interval could change which flow regime applies and thus which numeric limits or monitoring triggers are in effect.

candidates.exact_span: BOD        Biochemical oxygen demand (five-day unless noted otherwise)
candidates.computation_change_reason: Specifies that BOD limits default to the five-day test unless another duration is stated; interpreting BOD without this qualifier could pair reported measurements with the wrong analytical basis and change exceedance determinations.

candidates.exact_span: CBOD       Carbonaceous biochemical oxygen demand (five-day unless noted otherwise)
candidates.computation_change_reason: Same five-day default as BOD but for carbonaceous fraction; misidentifying CBOD versus BOD or the test duration could change which numeric limit is compared to reported results.

Defines BMP as a management plan rather than the more common 'practice'; if permit obligations reference BMP requirements, this expansion affects whether monitoring or implementation duties are plan-based versus practice-based.

Identifies the formal reporting vehicle for monitoring results; ambiguity about what constitutes a DMR versus other submissions could change whether monitoring was required to be reported and whether missing ordinary numeric results count as adequate evidence.

candidates.exact_span: mg/l       Milligrams per liter (one part per million)
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes the concentration unit for many enforceable limits; a different unit interpretation or conversion would change numeric compliance comparisons against reported measurements.

candidates.exact_span: ug/l       Micrograms per litter (one part per billion)
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defines microgram-per-liter scaling for trace parameters, but the spelling 'litter' instead of 'liter' introduces unit ambiguity that could alter limit-to-result conversions and whether very low reported values are treated as quantified or unresolved.

Sets the document's term for the lowest reliably quantified concentration; different treatment of values below MQL could change whether a numeric limit comparison is performed or whether the case is classified as missing/non-quantified evidence.

Reasonable-potential findings commonly trigger additional or more frequent monitoring; how this term is interpreted when cross-referenced elsewhere could change which monitoring requirements are deemed applicable for FY2025.
pH limits are expressed in standard units rather than mg/l; misapplying concentration units to pH measurements would change whether reported pH values exceed applicable limits.

WET is a distinct compliance parameter with pass/fail or numeric endpoints rather than conventional pollutant limits; interpreting WET obligations differently could change both applicable toxicity limits and required toxicity monitoring.
WLA ties discharge limits to water-quality allocations; if limits elsewhere are allocation-derived, a different reading of WLA could change which numeric cap applies at a discharge point.
